title: Electrical Comeback Credit: Workmanship Warranties Training Questions
content:
Under the Workmanship Warranties, an electrical comeback credit is taken off the electrical diagnostic charge on a Collision Lifetime Workmanship Warranty or Certified Structural Lifetime Warranty. The electrical comeback credit follows the remedy attempts on the coverage completed with the concern not resolved, network reworks and outside-shop repairs alike: two or more, the two-failure electrical credit of USD 25.00; exactly one, the one-failure electrical credit of USD 12.50; none, no electrical comeback credit.

## Questions

Q. Which remedy attempts are counted?
A. Every remedy attempt on the coverage whose completion recorded the concern as not resolved, whether it was a network rework or an outside-shop repair, and whichever concern on the coverage it was for.

Q. Do attempts completed with the concern resolved count?
A. No.

Q. Is there a time limit on the count?
A. No window applies; all such completions on the coverage are counted.

Q. What credit does each count give?

| Completions not resolved on the coverage | Electrical comeback credit |
|---|---|
| none | none |
| exactly one | USD 12.50 |
| two | USD 25.00 |
| three or more | USD 25.00 |

## Hypothetical illustration

A coverage shows one network rework completed not resolved, followed by an outside-shop repair completed not resolved on the same concern, and a later rework on another concern completed resolved. Two completions are not resolved: the credit is USD 25.00.
